item.text: Both backends currently only support single-field increments. Mongo can use one unordered atomic update per key; Redis needs a small Lua script inside a pipeline so each key’s fields are validated together before any `HINCRBY` runs. I’m adding shared input semantics to each implementation, including duplicate-key tuple merging and cache invalidation only for successful keys.

The implementations are in place. Mongo issues one `$inc` update per distinct key and retries duplicate-key upserts; Redis pipelines one Lua-backed update per key, which checks every current field and overflow before running any `HINCRBY`. I’m reviewing the diff and linting before I run the existing hash suite.
